analysis: The PR modifies only docs/architecture/inference.md. It changes no executable code, keys, endpoints or deployment settings. I examined the two base-text units (lines 1611-2365). The patch excerpt is truncated, so I could not see the full diff of the new inline video label bullet (head lines 1896-1899). Doc changes: (1) GLM5 video text now says variable-frame-rate MP4/QuickTime tracks are indexed at i/nominalFrameRate instead of refused with a 400; (2) a new bullet describes MediaIngest.admittedVideoDataURIHeaders, listing base64 data:video/mp4, x-m4v, quicktime and mov labels. These are documentation of provider-side media ingest behavior. They touch TB-003/TB-007 only tangentially (A-001 prompt confidentiality, T-050 plaintext video temp files). Nothing in the visible text shows a regression. The base text confirms that MemoryBackedVideoAsset keeps video payloads in memory and writes nothing to disk, consistent with T-050. Existing caps (25 MiB decoded, 600 s, 8 videos) stay as documented. The relaxed VFR handling in the GLM5 path could widen the media-decode surface. That depends on source changes outside this batch, and I have no evidence that they bypass the memory or size gates. The T-041 prefix-cache material is unchanged. Remaining integration questions: confirm that the actual Swift change to GLM5NextProcessor.decodeAsset and MediaIngest keeps the frame-count, decoded-byte and duration limits for VFR tracks, and that the data-URI label allowlist is enforced by content sniffing and not only by the label. Neither can be verified from this docs-only evidence.
